slides.texte_overlay:
Things every man
should own by 30
A good mattress and pillow. You spend a third of your life in bed. Good sleep changes your energy, your mood and your back more than any gadget.
One pair of quality leather shoes. Polished, resoled, kept for years. They look sharp with jeans or a suit, and they last far longer than three pairs of cheap ones.
A cast iron pan. Heavy, simple, almost indestructible. It cooks a perfect steak, gets better with age, and might outlive you.
A valid passport. Always ready, never expired. Being able to say yes to a last-minute trip or a work opportunity abroad is a quiet kind of freedom.
A learning habit you keep. I do five minutes a day on history, art or science, and it's the one thing I own that keeps getting more valuable.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It's the one thing I own that keeps getting more valuable.

slides.texte_overlay: Clean towels and sheets for guests. When a friend needs a place to stay, being ready to host them says you have your life in order and that your friends are always welcome.
A simple, reliable watch. Nothing flashy. Checking the time without picking up your phone keeps you present with people and looks effortlessly classic on any wrist.
